changes: Prevent a render-loop crash after ladder or climbable-surface dismount: reject non-finite stair path positions and never read an undefined transport tread .top.
Add a per-avatar Climb speed (0.20–4.00 m/s) to the existing compact Robot speed dropdown and shared slider; apply it to ascending, descending, and the authored climbing animation rate.
Persist Climb speed in scene creation, duplication, patches and multiplayer; enforce finite range validation in both backend scene endpoints.
Add executable regression coverage for invalid conveyor marker/path coordinates, missing stair segments, controlled climbing rates and persistence; preserve all existing stair and fall behaviours.
Prefer the authored Climbing Up Wall animation for every avatar climbing a ladder; keep Climbing Ladder and Climb as fallbacks when missing.
Add a compact opt-in Climbable checkbox on walls, models (including trees), and supported procedural objects, saved in scenes and preserved on duplication.
Manual Up/Down climbing now attaches to the actual nearby front-facing vertical surface mesh; Space detaches into Rapier gravity and top dismount requires physical support.
Include multi-client climb state, strict backend bool validation, browser cache mapping, and six executable surface-climb regression tests.
Add procedural Ladder immediately after Stairs advanced, with width, height, count/spacing-based rungs, textures, colour and per-bar static Rapier colliders.
Add manual Up/Down robot/ avatar climbing and Space release; select authored climbing animation where present and detect a real upper platform before dismount to Idle.
Replace robot portrait resize symbols with the exact supplied +/- SVGs and remove automatic icon decoration; compact Profile Edit Mode to a single label and pill.
Persist, duplicate, validate and archive ladders, add six ladder behaviour tests and advance all runtime/backend/cache version strings.
Route go_to commands for Advanced and Standard stairs around obstacles to the physically accessible low first-step entrance, instead of selecting the high or side face of a stair object.

Use actual staircase control points and complete world transform, preserve continuous obstacle-checked routes, and report blocked when the low entrance cannot be reached rather than claiming partial success.
Make robot command planning and arrival feedback distinguish reaching the low entrance from climbing; retain existing navigation and collision physics for unrelated objects.
Add five executed stair entry tests plus backend parser regression and refresh all browser/module/backend/release versions.

Default to Exploration Mode: a persistent, account-local iOS-style Profile Edit Mode switch controls editing windows and transform handles across the application without changing robot control, chat or scene physics.
Make the controlSwitcher draggable from unused surface space rather than a visible handle; retain interactive portraits/buttons and add compact minus/plus controls for portrait size.
Keep Rate and Pitch labels on one line in the robot voice panel.
Correct positive-yaw robot camera orientation to match panorama left-to-right stitching; verify six 60-degree views, seam blending and 360-degree wrap using synthetic source images.

Prevent automatic Pushing animation against props whose height is at most half the normalized avatar height; scale the threshold with each avatar and exclude objects on other floors or above the avatar.
Require the avatar to face the obstacle within 35 degrees and move forward into it; sideways motion and side-on robot-on-robot pushing cannot trigger automatic Push.

Measure proximity to the nearest world-space object surface, then require the Rapier character controller to report a collision against that precise Dynamic collider, rather than guessing from a broad bounding box or stalled movement.
Clear stale automatic object Pushing immediately when contact or direction becomes invalid; leave actual physics impulses, explicit combat moves, walking and collision geometry unchanged.
Add ten executable regression tests covering small bricks, height thresholds, frontal angles, sideways motion, wrong/no collision, far objects, scaled robots, and automatic contact cancellation.
Enable user-selected Trimesh collision for Dynamic, Static, and Kinematic scene objects, including remote-owned Dynamic objects. No rigid-body mode silently resets the collider choice.

Build the selected Trimesh with the existing transformed mesh geometry instead of forcing a box or compound collision; skip portal visual-only effect meshes and fall back to a box only when geometry creation fails or exceeds its safety budget.

Keep the collider choice when making an object pushable and preserve the current physics mode when cutting a cube opening; accept these combinations in backend scene persistence without changing robot character physics.
Add five dynamic/kinematic/static Trimesh regression tests, with fallback and default-box checks, and update the inspector runtime status for the actual collider choice.
All robot and avatar types now resume their prior active gait directly after a deliberate near-level jump (<=0.35m net elevation change), without additional Landing or forced Idle.
Rapier and non-Rapier jump completion paths retain per-robot run/walk/backward/strafe intent; genuine falls preserve Landing, Hard Landing, and extreme Falling Flat Impact then Stand Up.
Five new level-jump regression tests; existing 40-floor lifts, portals and network transport retained.

Raise lift limit from 12 to 40 floors consistently across editor, in-world button state, synchronized motion timeline, save validation, server WebSocket checks and high-rise shaft motion height (maximum 312 m with 8 m floors).
Arrange lift cabin floor buttons into a four-column, up-to-ten-row keypad for 13–40 floors; preserve existing single-column controls for 2–12 floors and optional per-floor landing call stations.

For a genuinely extreme fall over 8 m, play Falling Flat Impact after ground contact then Stand Up when both authentic clips exist; otherwise retain the one-shot Hard Landing to Idle, without duplicate recovery.
Add regression tests for 40th-floor travel and bounds, server validation, and fall clip availability and recovery sequencing.
Hard Landing has its own complete recovery: after a hard fall (>2.5 m), play Hard Landing then return directly to Idle/locomotion; do not queue a redundant Stand Up.
Ignore a legacy queued Stand Up after Hard Landing while preserving separate Stand Up recovery for severe combat impacts.
Add an executable hard-landing lifecycle regression and preserve all existing transport, portals, scene, backend and avatar files.
Simplify Portal inspector to one Width and one Height controlling the doorway and surrounding frame together, with automatic thickness and legacy saved geometry compatibility.
Replace seven duplicate geometry sliders with one contextual range slider linked to focused Width, Height, Depth, Delay or Opacity and compact numeric inputs.
Remove decorative colour pills and use one matching native portal colour input; simplify the compact layout while preserving portal effects, paired teleportation, WebXR and persistence.
Add executable portal UI and dimension regression tests and package as an incremented watcher-safe release.

Replace solid-looking Orb sphere and ring decorations with a luminous transparent event-horizon shader, an inward spiraling centered vortex throat, and contained star particles, preserving Entry/Exit visual distinction.
Keep Orb gates traversable: exclude spherical visual shells from Rapier collision and allow standing WebXR visitor capsules to activate the orb at natural headset height.
Add runtime regression checks for transparent orb materials, absence of opaque globes or decorative rings, shader animation across all four effect modes, and XR standing-body activation.
Restore paired gateways after a v0.2.120 runtime crash caused by calling non-existent THREE.Shape.containsPoint() during particle generation.
Generate sparkles with explicit point-in-polygon filtering; rebuild gate geometry transactionally and preserve existing saved portal meshes and settings when a visual construction step fails.

Smoke-test all 5 portal shapes, 4 visual effects, and Entry/Exit construction with simulated rendering failures; preserve the aperture-constrained effects, transport code, existing avatars and server storage compatibility.

Rebuild portal visuals so every effect is constrained to the actual aperture: door effects stay inside the opening, the rounded gate has a flat floor-aligned base, the floor field is a square floor portal, and the orb variant is a real sphere.
Add animated frame FX, better centered interior shaders, and sparkle / star-like particles so portals read as intentional in-world devices rather than loose planes or ring placeholders.
Preserve linked Entry/Exit transport behaviour, button triggering, persistence, and watcher-safe packaging while updating portal regression coverage for the rebuilt geometry.

Rework portal visuals so effect modes are materially different in-world: a clearly visible animated rainbow border, stronger glow/pulse treatments, and a new shader-driven mystery / reality-pull interior effect.

Compact the Portal inspector to match the rest of SOLVI properties: remove explanatory filler text, add one-line slider-plus-number controls, compact selects, curated colour swatches and a tighter layout with less vertical waste.
Keep paired portal transport, Entry/Exit linking, trigger modes and persistence intact while preserving watcher-safe packaging and versioned browser cache keys.

Reissue the v0.2.117 paired-portal geometry and animation update as v0.2.118 because the previous archive contained generated Python bytecode, which the deployment watcher correctly rejected at Git publishing.
Exclude all __pycache__ directories and .pyc/.pyo or other generated artifacts from the watcher ZIP and the checksum manifest; preserve the original application source and avatar bytes.
Refresh release, backend and Ubuntu installer versions, and all versioned browser import URLs and stylesheet cache keys for v0.2.118.
WebXR headset standing on a moving walkway or escalator is carried by the actual tread displacement, including X/Z travel and stair elevation; spectators outside the treads are not moved
Optional compact Start, Stop and Reverse controls at both walkway/escalator endpoints, with selectable left/right side positioning and mouse/WebXR controller-ray interaction
Server-authorized conveyor-control WebSocket messages synchronize direction and running state, and a saved command timestamp prevents older scene snapshots from reversing newer controls
Preserve the original robot rider, lifts, teleportation, and procedural-stair geometry; add tests for XR carrying, switch actions, state validation, and backwards compatibility
Reissue the v0.2.114 WebXR surface teleport improvements under a strictly newer release version after the watcher rejected re-deployment of v0.2.114
Refresh all browser import-map and CSS cache keys, backend health version, installer default version and release metadata; no change to XR teleport behaviour
WebXR teleport controller rays target actual nearby static/trimesh surfaces, stairs, moving walkways and lift cabin floors instead of only the world floor
Apply XR teleport limits to controller range and headset-to-target distance, reject steep surfaces and large downward jumps, and provide a personal 2–20 m limit in World Settings
Track XR standing-surface elevation across surface teleports, lifts and paired portals; render teleport rings at true hit height and orientation
Ensure moving walkway and escalator riders are carried by the owning client using geometric tread support, authorized conveyor robot-motion packets, and shared visual marker phase
Carry the WebXR headset vertically with a moving lift cabin using tracking reference-space offsets while the viewer is inside its footprint
Restore vertical displacement for WebXR portal teleportation and preserve local entry height at the paired exit, without changing ordinary ground-ray teleportation
Lift passengers no longer enter airborne gravity when a different client commands downward or reverse travel
The lift carries both the robot transform and Rapier body before running character physics and maintains grounded support while aboard
Remote lift start packets wait for the rider-aware transport tick; remote y corrections cannot fight the active cabin
Robots can still jump or walk out of the cabin, releasing the support attachment
Lift starts, stops and arrivals now use a server-authorized event and persistent motion timeline instead of frequent position snapshots
Lift clients animate the same height, floor readout, landing buttons, shaft and collision position without jumping on scene revisions
Robot riders are predicted locally and owner pose updates include lift elevation; scene persistence remains ownership-checked
Robot control switcher is draggable with 25% larger portraits, active-selection highlight and scene-to-control synchronization
Add paired portal Entry and Exit, each movable independently in the realm
True doorway frames with static piecewise colliders, colour, texture and opacity
Automatic or button-triggered portal teleport with bounded delay, scene mouse and WebXR controls
Robot/object and XR/free-camera transport, physics sync, loop cooldown, Web Audio chime and portal glow
Reduce z-fighting on adjacent procedural stairs, roof/wall panels and overlays
Add opt-in floor-call stations beside the landing exit at every level of a procedural lift, with compact red numbered buttons and configurable left/right placement.
Keep landing-call stations stationary while the lift cabin moves, with an orange requested-floor indication and green arrived-floor indication.
Support mouse clicks and WebXR controller-ray selection using the existing permission-checked lift movement and saved destination action.
Expose Call button at each level and Button side inside the compact Lift stops and cabin settings; preserve existing lifts with calls disabled by default.
Validate and persist the call-button configuration, accept earlier five-field lift settings, and add focused source/runtime regression tests.
Add two small in-world lift control columns (inside and outside cabin) with numbered switches for each configured level.
Use green idle, red requested destination, and orange passing-floor feedback, plus a continuously updated large floor digit inside the cabin.
Allow ordinary pointer clicking and WebXR controller-ray selection, routing both through owner/permission-checked lift transport and scene persistence.
Play quiet synthetic Web Audio start and arrival jingles after an activated button press; no external audio downloads.
Update only controls/display textures and colours during lift movement; preserve riders, existing kinematic collision and lift settings.
Fix lift rider movement crash from plain {x,y,z} delta incorrectly treated as THREE.Vector3; keep owned robot kinematic bodies aligned during ascent and return.
Update lift kinematic platform body position with each moved frame to keep collision state aligned with rendered cabin.
Provide missing square.svg used by geometry icons to eliminate 404s.
Associate administrator and Tripo password fields with forms and add accessible admin username hints.
Add executable lift rider regression tests for moving up/down, dynamic objects, malformed deltas and source wiring.
Add Stairs advanced to Office Space with compact collapsible railing, rods/posts, roof/tunnel, supporting posts, step material and texture controls.
Add Escalators and Moving walkways with configurable speed/direction and contact-based movement of locally owned robots and loose dynamic objects, using separate geometric treads and physics.
Add Lifts with an open-ended cabin, two through twelve levels, floor-height/width controls, level landing frames and Start/Stop commands for kinematic travel.
Persist/validate new parametric settings, lift destination/current height, undo/redo snapshots and scene/archive metadata; avoid unnecessary collider rebuilds from travel-only state updates.
Add eight focused geometry, transport math, backend wiring and persistence regressions and bound test-runner concurrency for reliable watcher validation.
Robot portrait selector remains visible above Camera Follow, with correct active-robot highlighting. Selecting a robot now activates arrow-key control independently of Properties selection.
Video recording from chat or My Camera opens a live preview; capture does not begin until the user presses Start. Pause, resume, stop, discard, chat, scene and surface sharing remain available.
Chat audio and video attachments use slim shared custom controls, time/seek/mute/fullscreen, compact download/delete actions and no raw filename or native player bar.

Chat fetches metadata instead of loading entire recordings. On Play, authenticated 15-minute HLS access is requested; native HLS or locally bundled hls.js plays the stream; direct blob playback is a failure fallback.
Media deletion requires uploader/admin authorization and rejects scene, environment, profile and bookmarked references; linked chat attachments are unlinked on success.
Realm transitions: defer replacing the old scene until the next realm data arrives, reject stale responses and build objects in frame-sized batches
World Settings: avoid redundant floor-texture reapplication, physics resets and scene-list rebuilds when no setting changed
Chat: render the latest 180 entries initially, progressively load older history, yield frames during long timelines and retain full transcript exports
Chat controls: center the downward navigation arrow and enlarge participant avatars by 50 percent
Robot Control: replace the visible dropdown with selectable robot portrait/initial buttons above the controller
My Camera: Record, Pause/Resume and Stop buttons reuse the active webcam video; recorded clips can be attached to chat, added to the scene or drawn onto a selected cube/plane as a media frame

Virtual view capture: optional canvas captureStream recording with MediaRecorder on supported browsers, with a 15 fps capture target and conservative video bitrate; not guaranteed to include Quest passthrough
Media frames: choose realm chat attachments, camera-bookmark screenshots, uploaded media, live webcam photos or a recorded webcam clip
Chat composer: show a live webcam preview during video recording and recorded video playback after stopping
Procedural walls: convert individual wall segments to static editable cubes with true O-key cuttable openings and trimesh colliders
New robot messages: progressive typing and a subtle bubble entrance animation (history and reduced-motion users unaffected)
Compact chat audio play/seek/mute UI; signed expiring HLS VOD access for audio and video on native-HLS browsers; authenticated blob fallback elsewhere
Freeze camera during drawing and correct pointer-to-world ray mapping
Use analytic cube face raycast for openings and media rectangles (including pre-cut cubes)
Editable and persistent text geometry: content, font, size, extrusion and bevel with local typeface assets
Add regression tests for text geometry validation and camera lock
